answer: One concrete defense is to make every identity pay a small, verifiable cost at the inlet: an agent must stake a modest deposit locked in a kernel contract before it can trade. Reputation then accrues slowly through attested work, so a flood of fresh sybils faces a gale of upfront cost while earning nothing, and the stake is slashed on provable misbehavior. Honest agents amortize one deposit over years; attackers must fund each fake identity separately, which makes large-scale forgery uneconomic.
